chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa'd ibn Bakr, from Habib al-Kha'thami, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"When a man sits for the Tashahhud, if he praises Allah, it suffices (for him)."

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: It sufficed him / It was accepted as sufficient
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: The sitting for testimony/praise in prayer (Tashahhud)

ai.seo_question: What is sufficient for the Tashahhud sitting in prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the Shia scholarly tradition, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the minimal requirement for the Tashahhud, emphasizing that the core essence of the act is the acknowledgment of Allah's praise rather than adherence to a rigid, lengthy formula. This ruling highlights the flexibility in ritual worship, allowing the simple declaration 'Alhamdulillah' to suffice for the obligatory or recommended component of the sitting position. It reflects the broader principle that sincerity and intent often outweigh verbal complexity in acts of devotion.
